solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 16 across to 15); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Want jet to drop its nose?

indicators.note: a word's nose is its front, so dropping it removes the first letter of the jet colour word

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an aircraft should dip its nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' looks like an aircraft, which the nose supports; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to be without it, a synonym of lacking.

clue.text: One boy probing endowment's lawfulness

indicators.note: something probing goes into the other piece

parts.note: a legacy is an endowment left in a will
one is the Roman numeral I
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad investigates whether a bequest is legal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probing' means going into: the one and the boy push into the endowment, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimacy is the quality of being lawful or legally valid.

clue.text: Tea appearing by military service entrance

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits beside the other

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
RM is the Royal Marines, a branch of the forces

explanation.surface: Tea is served by the gate of an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to delight or bewitch them, a synonym of charming them.

clue.text: Sweet coating Briton cooked chip in

indicators.note: one piece covers the other, so the sweet word wraps round the cooked letters

parts.note: sweet means cute

indicators.note: something cooked has been worked over, so the letters of Briton are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British cook coats potato chips in something sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' makes ONTRIB, and 'coating' has the sweet word wrap round it. 'Chip in' looks like a fried potato but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an idiom for adding one's share, the same as contributing.

clue.text: Finished version is something generating interest?

parts.note: over means finished
a draft is a version of a text

explanation.surface: A final draft is something that should grab a reader's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' seems to mean fascination, but it is the charge a bank makes.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn account accrues interest charges, a whimsical description of borrowing.

clue.text: Revolting kid and computing bores may be so

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a kid is a lad
IT is information technology, computing

explanation.surface: A nasty child and computer nerds can be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgusting but reverses LADIT. 'Bores' are not dull people but surge waves on rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore is a wave that runs up a river on a rising tide.

clue.text: The writer's not in a dead end

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's is I'm, I am
passé means out of fashion, no longer in

explanation.surface: A writer insists they are not stuck in a dead end.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock or situation with no way forward.

clue.text: Spurs' middle defender moves? Not supply enough

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter
moves signals the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: The Tottenham centre-back is on the move. Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle' picks U from 'Spurs''. 'Moves' rearranges DEFENDER into NDERFEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To underfeed is to give too little food, so not providing enough.

clue.text: Top broken off more modern jug

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: more modern means newer

explanation.surface: A modern jug has had its lid broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed water jug.

clue.text: Busy European Court overwhelmed by drunken noise

indicators.note: one piece swamped by another lies within it

parts.note: hic is the sound of a drunk's hiccup

explanation.surface: A European court is drowned out by drunken racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwhelmed by' means swamped inside: the hiccup sound swallows the European court.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic means frantically busy and full of activity.

clue.text: Places for final rest stop in Kentish Town

parts.note: graves are where the dead are laid to rest
a stop is an end

explanation.surface: A traveller hunts for a last overnight halt in a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is also a London district, but here it means a town in Kent: Gravesend sits on the Thames estuary in the English county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is an example of a town in Kent, the English county on the Thames estuary.

clue.text: Minister to cut, dressing back of hand

indicators.note: a dressing is wrapped round a wound, so the cutting word goes round the letter

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told to cut a bandage for the back of an injured hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back of' picks D from 'hand', which sits inside PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain, a minister of religion especially in the armed forces.

clue.text: Prepared to drive round point on motorway that's inclined

indicators.note: the golfing word goes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a golfer who has teed up is ready to drive

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: M stands for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A driver gets ready to steer round a junction on a motorway that slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared to drive' is golf, not cars: a ball on a tee. 'Round' and 'on' place the motorway and point inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tempted means being disposed or inclined to do something.

clue.text: Polish vice chancellor finally has energy

parts.note: lust is one of the deadly sins, a vice

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word chancellor

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A vice-chancellor of a university turns out to be lively and Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice chancellor' reads as one title but splits: 'vice' gives LUST, 'chancellor finally' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the sheen or gloss that polishing gives a surface.

clue.text: Looked around extremely romantically and enthusiastically if so

definitions.text: Looked around extremely romantically and enthusiastically if so

indicators.note: the looking word goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: looked means stared

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last, of each word

explanation.surface: Someone gazing about in a dreamy, eager way would be starry-eyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the end letters of the two adverbs, and 'around' sets the looking word round them. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means naively romantic or idealistic, gazing dreamily.

clue.text: Riotous cheering met Man United's historic capitulation in Europe?

indicators.note: riotous suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Man U is the usual short form of Manchester United

explanation.surface: Wild celebrations greeted a Manchester United team that collapsed in a European tie.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1938 Munich Agreement saw Britain and France let Hitler take Czech lands; the football surface plays on Munich, scene of United's 1958 air disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1938 pact is the byword for appeasement, the Western powers giving way to Hitler.

clue.text: Horseman's heading off before horse trial

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second in a down entry
a heading is a first letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior, a horseman
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A rider sets off ahead of a horse trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' looks equestrian, but it is the definition: an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a harrowing ordeal or trial.

clue.text: Drug wrapped in brightly coloured newspaper is something for a key player

indicators.note: one piece wrapped in another sits inside it

parts.note: red is a bright colour
E is slang for ecstasy
an organ is a newspaper or journal

explanation.surface: Drugs are wrapped in a garish newspaper for an important player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key player' looks like a star athlete; it means a keyboard player.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ is a keyboard instrument, so something a keyboard player plays.

clue.text: Fashion accessory's cooler, keeping the gear amazingly with it

indicators.note: one word keeps the other inside it, holding it within

parts.note: cooler means colder

indicators.note: amazingly signals the letters are jumbled into a surprising order

explanation.surface: A stylish accessory is said to be cool, holding the gear and being fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazingly' makes IGARETTEH from the gear and it; 'keeping' puts that inside the cooler word. 'With it' looks like 'fashionable' but only supplies fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The long holder was a classic glamour accessory of 1920s and later fashion.

clue.text: Artist: a painter lifting hearts in spring

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting means reading upward, backwards
in places the letter inside the jumping word

parts.note: a spring is a leap
H is short for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A painter is cheered by springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: H inside LEAP makes LEAHP; 'lifting' turns it up to PHAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was an Italian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Like a chestnut horse that stops running to lad

indicators.note: a stopper fills a gap inside something, so the letter goes inside
running suggests the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, H

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse halts as it runs toward a stable lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' turns TO LAD into OLDAT, with H inside. A chestnut is also a stale joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat means stale and overfamiliar, like a tired old joke.

clue.text: Silly phrases from the right papers

indicators.note: reading from the right means taking the letters backwards

parts.note: to phrase something is to put it, as in putting it nicely
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Daft headlines appear in right-wing newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the right' reverses PUTS to make STUP. 'Papers' looks like newspapers but means identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and silly are close synonyms for foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Social clubs toured by underworld circle

indicators.note: something toured is gone round, so the other letters surround it

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a circle looks like the letter O
C is short for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: Gangland figures do the rounds of nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social' is a noun, a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance party, a kind of social gathering.

clue.text: Peaceful ring road runs into cathedral city

parts.note: a ring is the round letter O

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so the letter is put inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A quiet ring road runs into a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England; 'into' puts runs inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means calm and well behaved, the opposite of disorderly, so peaceful.

clue.text: Little jumper I'm amazed is loose-fitting

parts.note: roo is a short informal word for a kangaroo
my is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at a baggy children's sweater. In British English a jumper is a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater but is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, so a garment with room is loose-fitting.

clue.text: Finally cut lavish bonus

indicators.note: the final letter of the luxurious word is cut off

parts.note: plush means luxurious, lavish

explanation.surface: A generous bonus has finally been reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or bonus.

clue.text: Asian city, Seoul, has amazing walls

indicators.note: the words wall in the answer, enclosing it within their letters

explanation.surface: Seoul is praised for its remarkable city walls.
explanation.walkthrough: Seoul looks like the city wanted, but it is part of the text that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa, capital of Tibet, is a city in Asia.

clue.text: Something that shows a politician's party in agreement

parts.note: a sign is something that shows or indicates
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A sign shows which party a politician belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' seems to belong to the politician but belongs to the definition. TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A signatory is one who signs a treaty or contract, so a party to the agreement.

clue.text: List characters sure to be fascinated

parts.note: to spell is to list a word's letters in order
bound to means certain to

explanation.surface: Someone reading out letters is certain to be enthralled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spellbound means held in rapt attention, entranced.

clue.text: Daisy's outside with Bill — they're a couple

indicators.note: the outside of a word means its first and last letters

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Daisy is out with Bill on a date as a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like Daisy is out of doors; it picks D and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyad is a group of two, a pair.
